title: FormSchema.onChange is a declared public callback the form renderer never calls — authoring it is a silent no-op
body:
Filed unassigned per Prime Directive #10, found while fixing #4247 (the gated-options cascade clear lives in the same effect region of `form.tsx`). Not in that card's scope.

## What happens

`FormSchema` declares four lifecycle callbacks in `@object-ui/types` (`packages/types/src/form.ts`, `interface FormSchema` at line 1055):

```
onSubmit?: (data: Record"<"string, any">") =" ">" void | Promise"<"void">";
onChange?: (data: Record"<"string, any">") =" ">" void;
onDirtyChange?: (isDirty: boolean) =" ">" void;
onCancel?: () =" ">" void;
```

(generics spelled defensively here — the body sanitizer eats bare angle brackets)

The renderer destructures all four off `schema` together, in one block at `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx:534-537`:

```
onSubmit: onSubmitProp,
onChange: onChangeProp,
onDirtyChange: onDirtyChangeProp,
onCancel: onCancelProp,
```

Three of them are then wired. `onChangeProp` is never referenced again — the destructure is its only occurrence in the file:

```
$ grep -c onSubmitProp      form.tsx   -> 3
$ grep -c onDirtyChangeProp form.tsx   -> 5
$ grep -c onCancelProp      form.tsx   -> 4
$ grep -c onChangeProp      form.tsx   -> 1     (the destructure itself)
```

So a consumer that wires `onChange` on a form schema is handed a typed, documented, autocompleted API that does nothing at all. There is no warning, no dev-mode notice, and no type error — the declaration says it is supported.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a deletion in passing

Two readings, and they need a maintainer rather than a guess:

- **Wire it** — the value-change channel is the one lifecycle hook missing from a form that already publishes submit / dirty / cancel, and `onDirtyChange` right beside it proves the subscription plumbing (a `form.watch` equivalent) already exists here. If any consumer wants live values, this is the declared place for them.
- **Retire it** — declared-but-unenforced is the enforce-or-remove family (ADR-0049 in the sibling repo): if nothing pulls on it, the honest fix is removing the declaration so it stops advertising a capability that is not there.

Which one is right depends on whether there is real business pull for a live value channel on `FormSchema`, which is a product call. Note the two are not symmetric in cost: wiring it is additive and safe, while removing it is a public type change on `@object-ui/types`.

## Reachability

Any consumer authoring `onChange` on a form schema — the prop is public, exported and documented. I did not find an in-repo caller, which is why this reads as dormant drift rather than a live break; a downstream consumer of `@object-ui/types` cannot be checked from here.
